statement: Several research questions on covers remain open. A first question is how efficiently we can construct a small cover of size Op|D|entw q. Our current construction takes time Op|QpDq|q, ˚ which can be as large as Ωp|D|ρ q. It would be interesting to explore whether it is possible to reduce this time down to Op|D|subw q using the PANDA algorithm as a blackbox. A second direction is to consider algorithms that compute the instance-optimal cover (instead of the worst-case optimal). It is likely that this becomes a computationally hard problem – especially when we consider multiple tree decompositions – however, there might be cases where the problem of finding the smallest cover is tractable.
context: In this paper, we have shown that by generalizing covers to depend on multiple tree decompositions, we can construct covers of asymptotically smaller size. We have also provided matching worst-case lower bounds for general degree constraints. Several research questions on covers remain open. A first question is how efficiently we can construct a small cover of size Op|D|entw q. Our current construction takes time Op|QpDq|q, ˚ which can be as large as Ωp|D|ρ q. It would be interesting to explore whether it is possible to reduce this time down to Op|D|subw q using the PANDA algorithm as a blackbox. A second direction is to consider algorithms that compute the instance-optimal cover (instead of the worst-case optimal). It is likely that this becomes a computationally hard problem – especially when we consider multiple tree decompositions – however, there might be cases where the problem of finding the smallest cover is tractable. Finally, it is possible to consider a variant of a generalized cover where the output of each decomposition is disjoint from each other. In other words, we want QpDq to be partitioned into tIi uiPT such that each Ii has a cover Ki w.r.t. the decomposition i. Such a “disjoint cover” tKi uiPT would allow us to construct a semiring circuit for any semiring, even one that is non-idempotent. The current greedy algorithm, however, does not have the disjointness guarantee and thus it is not clear how we can construct disjoint covers of small size.
